title: A settle the busy store deferred is booked when its step ends, not left held
evidence: packages/kernel/src/spend/meter.ts settle: holds.delete on 'deferred'; per-step createSettler never flushed after the step; packages/kernel/test/job.spend.test.ts new case: usd 0 -> 0.03, held -> settled, lateWrites 1
body:
## Summary
stepMeter dropped a hold whose settle the store deferred; the pending settle lived only in the per-step settler and was never applied.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/spend/meter.ts removed the hold from `holds` on a deferred settle; job-run.ts book's lapseOpen never saw it, so the reservation stayed held forever and the vendor figure never booked. open() now returns pending settles with their entries and lapseOpen settles them.

## Flow
- live metered step; spend.settle tx answers unavailable
- settler queues it, meter forgets the hold
- booking tx: lapseOpen(meter.open()) settles it

## Expected impact
Job spend and the period window read what the vendor charged. Could break: nothing; settle is idempotent.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a deferred settle is never lost
Before: job usd 0, reservation held forever
After: usd 0.03, settled, lateWrites 1
Method: gate - new job.spend case, seeded red on HEAD
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A pending settle that can never apply blocks every later settle; lapseOpen drops it uncounted
instrument: packages/kernel/test/spend.test.ts case: createSettler over a one-shot unavailable tx; defer r1; release r1 directly; settle r2 -> today r2 fails with r1's 'released cannot become settled' and stays held; after: r2 applied, r1 dropped and counted (counter + event). Plus a stepMeter case where the pending hold is released before the booking: lapseOpen today ignores the refused settle with no counter.
evidence:
packages/kernel/src/spend/settler.ts run(): `if (!s.ok) throw s.error` for each taken pending, so the whole tx (and the new settle) rolls back and the queue is kept
packages/kernel/src/spend/meter.ts lapseOpen: `if (!s.ok && s.error.code !== "refused") throw` - a refused pending settle is skipped with no counter
body:
## Summary
In packages/kernel/src/spend/settler.ts, a queued settle whose reservation was closed meanwhile (released, expired) throws in every later run(), so each later settle on that settler fails and its hold stays held; meter.ts lapseOpen skips the same case silently.

## Description
run() replays every pending settle before the new one inside one transaction and throws on the first non-ok. A pending settle that cannot ever apply (reservation released by an operator, expired by the v1 port, not-found) therefore poisons the queue: the store is fine, but every new settle returns that error and its own hold stays held, counting against the ceiling. lapseOpen (this round's 89b0d993) ignores `refused` for a pending settle as it does for a lapse, so the vendor's figure is dropped with no counter. cost-metering usage-ledgers: 'count every dropped write'. Fixed: a pending settle that fails non-unavailable is dropped from the queue with a counter and an event, and the rest of the transaction proceeds; lapseOpen counts the same.

## Flow
- meteredCall r1: settle deferred (busy)
- operator or v1 reclaim closes r1
- meteredCall r2: settle -> r1 replay throws -> r2 not settled, error to caller
- every later settle on this settler fails the same way

## Expected impact
Later calls book what they cost instead of failing their settle; a dropped vendor figure is visible as a count. Could break: a reader of the queue that expects a failed replay to stay queued (none in tree).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one unappliable late write does not block the others, and is counted
Before: 1 unappliable pending -> every later settle fails (walked, settler.ts run)
After: later settles apply; 1 dropped write counted
Method: simulation - walked run() and lapseOpen; needs a counter name and event shape decided with the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none

title: An over-budget route leaves no router.* decision event
instrument: packages/kernel/test/dryrun.test.ts: the over-budget case's event list today is [spend.refused, receipt.released]; after: a router.* event (routed with hold refused, or refused reason over-budget) naming the provider the decision chose, beside spend.refused. Update the pinned sequence and check lib/ledger readers of router.* for the new reason value.
evidence:
packages/kernel/src/router/reserve.ts routeAndReserve: `return { kind: "over-budget", routed: out, error: r.error }` returns before any append(router.*)
packages/kernel/test/dryrun.test.ts:145 pins events [spend.refused, receipt.released]
body:
## Summary
routeAndReserve records router.routed or router.refused for every decision except the one the ceiling refused: an over-budget outcome writes only spend.refused, which does not name the provider or the trail.

## Description
model-routing's decision record ('which model served this call and why includes none and why', quoted in reserve.ts's own JSDoc) has a gap exactly where money stops a call: the route WAS decided (provider, model, rung, trail) and then refused by the hold, and the only event is spend.refused on the reservation subject, carrying totals but no routing. Fixed: append a router.* event for the over-budget case (a `router.refused` with reason `over-budget`, or `router.routed` with `hold: refused`). RefusalReason has no such member and the dryrun test pins the sequence, so this changes an in-tree event vocabulary.

## Flow
- live image request, imaging-usd near its ceiling
- route chooses google; reserve refuses
- events: spend.refused only - which provider would have served is lost

## Expected impact
A Ledger reader can say which vendor a money stop blocked. Could break: any reader that treats router.refused as a routing refusal only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every routing decision has its record
Before: over-budget decisions with a router.* event: 0 of 1 outcome kinds
After: 1 of 1
Method: simulation - read the three return paths; the event shape is a vocabulary choice the instrument must make
Result: better
Gate: none

packages/producers/src/extract/define.ts:129 translates `s.basis === "estimated" ? "estimate" : "vendor"` by hand
body:
## Summary
The ledger's basis is free text and only the exact word 'estimate' books a figure as the model's; the kernel's own Quote vocabulary spells it 'estimated', so passing a quote's basis through books an estimate as real money.

## Description
Two vocabularies for one fact inside one package: pricing/quote.ts (vendor-reported/estimated/unpriced) and spend/ledger.ts SettleEntry.basis (string; 'vendor', 'estimate', 'credits', 'seat' in use). bookIn and the projection's meterOf (basis = 'estimate') key on the exact string. extract/define.ts already hand-translates; every other producer happens to write 'estimate'. Probe: grep of in-tree SettleEntry literals found no 'estimated' today, so the defect is latent. Fixed: a closed union type (typecheck is the verifier) or a mapping from CostBasis at the door.

## Flow
- a producer books { amount, basis: quote.basis }
- basis 'estimated' !== 'estimate'
- spend.booked cost.src 'real'; meterOf basis 'reported'

## Expected impact
An estimate can never be shown as a receipt by a spelling. Could break: callers in lib/ and packages/producers that pass other words.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one basis vocabulary at the ledger door
Before: 2 vocabularies, exact-string match; 1 hand translation
After: 1 closed type; 0 translations
Method: probe - grep of every SettleEntry literal in tree; the type change spans other contexts
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The image gate's hold ignores the request's size and holds $0 when no image row is priced
evidence:
packages/kernel/src/router/reserve.ts holdFor image: `dearest === undefined ? 0 : dearest.usdPerUnit * Math.max(req.units, 1)`
packages/kernel/src/pricing/quote.ts dearestRate ignores atSize; PRICE_TABLE google gemini-3.1-flash-image atSize 1K $0.045 ('Nano Banana roughly doubles per size step', quote.ts header)
body:
## Summary
holdFor's image hold is dearestRate('image') x units: the 1K Google figure whatever size the request pins, and $0 if no image row were priced.

## Description
quote() refuses to carry the 1K figure to a 2K render ('a fiction'), but the pre-call gate does exactly that, so a 2K or 4K Google batch is held at roughly half or a quarter of what it costs. And if every image row went unpriced or dated out, dearestRate is undefined and the hold is $0 - 'unpriced is not free' broken at the gate. Holding more is a tightening, but the figure for 2K is unmeasured: choosing a multiplier, or refusing sized requests, is inventing a price or changing what is offered. v1 (lib/imaging/budget.ts estimatePendingUsd) has the same rule.

## Flow
- image generate, size 2K, units 4
- hold 4 x $0.045 = $0.18
- vendor bills roughly 2x per size step

## Expected impact
The imaging ceiling would hold what a sized batch costs. Could break: a hold that refuses work the ceiling would in fact fit.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the gate never holds less than a call can cost
Before: sized requests held at the 1K rate; no-row case holds $0
After: operator's rule: a measured 2K row, a declared multiplier, or a refusal
Method: simulation - walked holdFor and dearestRate; the missing figure is a price nobody measured
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

Until the cutover, a hold-rule change must be made twice or diverges silently. Which copy is the authority, and when the lib gates move onto routeAndReserve, is the migration plan's call (docs/next/migration-plan.md), not a sweep's.

## Flow

- grep hold rules in lib/: 3

## Evaluation

Before: 1 kernel copy with 0 production callers + 3 live v1 copies
After: 1
Method: probe - grep of callers; the cutover is an architecture decision
Result: unmeasurable

## Summary
Moving the TTL check before the body check would let an aged key be reused for a different request.

## Description
The header's rule is that a key names one request; answering a different body under it is the silent wrong answer the conflict exists to stop. Reordering loosens it.

## Flow

- today conflict; reordered: fresh claim

## Expected impact
None wanted.

## Evaluation

Before: conflict (correct per the header)
After: fresh claim for a different body (looser)
Method: probe - read the header's rule and the pinned case
Result: not-better
Gate: policy-loosen
